title: Meiosis, Inheritance and Genetic Crosses
seo_title: Year 12 Biology: Cell Division and Inheritance Worksheets (Australian Curriculum)
standard_code: Biology Unit 3: DNA, genes and the continuity of life
standard_text: Meiosis and the sources of genetic variation; alleles, genotype and phenotype; monohybrid and dihybrid crosses; dominance, codominance and incomplete dominance; sex linkage and pedigrees; the chi-squared test. (Senior Secondary Biology, Unit 3: Heredity and continuity of life)
meta_desc: Free Year 12 Biology worksheets on inheritance: meiosis, crossing over, alleles, Punnett squares, dihybrid crosses, codominance, sex linkage, pedigrees and the chi-squared test. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Sex-linked recessive traits are more common in males (XY).
body_html:
How to think about it

Meiosis makes haploid gametes; crossing over and independent assortment produce new combinations of alleles. The genotype (alleles) with the environment gives the phenotype.

Use Punnett squares for crosses: Aa × Aa gives 3 : 1; AaBb × AaBb gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 (unless genes are linked). In codominance both alleles show (blood group AB). X-linked recessive traits appear more in males. The chi-squared test checks if observed ratios fit expected ones.

Example

Bb × bb: proportion bb?

Bb × bb gives Bb, Bb, bb, bb

Answer: 1/2

Example

Carrier mother XᴴXʰ × normal father XᴴY. Chance a son has haemophilia?

sons get X from mother: Xᴴ or Xʰ

Answer: 1/2

Common mistakes

  • Thinking dominant means more common.
  • Forgetting that sons get their X chromosome from their mother.
  • Using a 3 : 1 ratio for a test cross: it gives 1 : 1.

faq.a: Crossing over swaps sections between homologous chromosomes, and independent assortment shuffles which chromosome of each pair goes into a gamete.

faq.q: What does a chi-squared test tell you?
faq.a: Whether the difference between observed and expected numbers is small enough to be due to chance (compare χ² with the critical value).

items.q: A diploid body cell of a plant has 20 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 10.

items.q: What is a test cross?
c: crossing an organism of unknown genotype with a homozygous recessive
items.e: Any recessive offspring show the unknown parent is heterozygous.

items.q: A diploid body cell of an animal has 14 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 7.

items.q: A species has 5 pairs of chromosomes. How many different chromosome combinations can occur in zygotes from random fertilisation (ignoring crossing over)?
What is crossing over?
c: separation of sister chromatids in mitosis
exchange of sections between homologous chromosomes during prophase I of meiosis
items.e: It makes new combinations of alleles.

items.q: A gamete of a species of fruit fly has 2 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 4.

items.q: Which is a polygenic trait?
items.e: Many genes plus environment give continuous variation.

items.q: A gamete of an animal has 6 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 12.

items.q: A chimpanzee egg and sperm each have 24 chromosomes. How many does the fertilised egg have?
What does homozygous mean?
c: having two identical alleles of a gene
items.e: BB and bb are homozygous.

items.q: A diploid body cell of a plant has 16 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in one of its gametes?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: 8.

items.q: A potato body cell has 48 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 24.

items.q: A corn body cell has 20 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
A cat body cell has 38 chromosomes (2n). How many are in each egg or sperm cell?
items.e: Meiosis halves the number: n = 19.

items.q: What is an allele?
c: a section of a chromosome with many genes
a different form of the same gene
items.e: For example, alleles for blood group A, B and O.

items.q: A corn egg and sperm each have 10 chromosomes. How many does the fertilised egg have?
A diploid cell of a fish has 6 chromosomes. How many different combinations of chromosomes can its gametes have by independent segregation?
items.e: With n = 3 pairs, combinations = 2n = 8.

items.q: A gamete of a species of fruit fly has 4 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are in a cell after mitosis in this organism?
items.e: Body cells are diploid (2n): 8.

items.q: A fruit fly body cell has 8 chromosomes. How many homologous pairs is that?
items.e: 8 ÷ 2 = 4 pairs.

items.q: In a pedigree, two unaffected parents have an affected child. What does this show?
c: the trait is recessive and both parents are carriers
items.e: A dominant trait would show in a parent.

items.q: In humans, the cross AaBb × AaBb is made. What proportion of the offspring show both dominant phenotypes?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for AaBb × AaBb and count the matching boxes: 916.

items.q: In snapdragons, the cross Cᴿ Cᵂ × Cᴿ Cᴿ (codominant) is made. What proportion of the offspring are red (Cᴿ Cᴿ)?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Cᴿ Cᵂ × Cᴿ Cᴿ (codominant) and count the matching boxes: 12.

items.q: Why are sex-linked recessive conditions such as red–green colour blindness more common in males?
c: the allele is on the Y chromosome
males have one X chromosome, so a single recessive allele is expressed
items.e: Females need two copies to show the trait.

items.q: In humans, the cross Iᴬ Iᴬ × Iᴮ Iᴼ (blood groups) is made. What proportion of the offspring have blood group A?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Iᴬ Iᴬ × Iᴮ Iᴼ (blood groups) and count the matching boxes: 12.

items.q: In fruit flies, the cross Aa × Aa is made. What proportion of the offspring show the dominant phenotype?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Aa × Aa and count the matching boxes: 34.

items.q: In pea, tall (T) is dominant over dwarf (t). Two heterozygous tall plants (Tt × Tt) give 36 offspring. How many are expected to be dwarf?
items.e: Tt × Tt gives 3 tall : 1 dwarf, so ¼ of 36 = 9.

items.q: How many chromosomes are in a human gamete?
items.e: Gametes are haploid.

items.q: In humans, the cross Iᴬ Iᴼ × Iᴮ Iᴼ (blood groups) is made. What proportion of the offspring have blood group O?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Iᴬ Iᴼ × Iᴮ Iᴼ (blood groups) and count the matching boxes: 14.

items.q: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is test-crossed with a dwarf plant (tt), giving 48 offspring. How many are expected to be dwarf?
items.e: Tt × tt gives 1 tall : 1 dwarf: 24.

items.q: In mice, the cross AA × aa is made. What proportion of the offspring show the recessive phenotype?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for AA × aa and count the matching boxes: 0.

items.q: In rabbits, the cross AA × aa is made. What proportion of the offspring show the recessive phenotype?
items.e: Draw a Punnett square for AA × aa and count the matching boxes: 0.

items.e: Draw a Punnett square for AaBb × aabb and count the matching boxes: 14.

items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Aa × Aa and count the matching boxes: 12.

items.e: The genotypic ratio of a monohybrid cross is 1 : 2 : 1.

items.e: Draw a Punnett square for Aa × Aa and count the matching boxes: 34.

items.q: What is the phenotype of an organism?
c: the DNA sequence of one gene
its observable characteristics, produced by genotype and environment
items.e: Genotype + environment → phenotype.

items.q: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is test-crossed with a dwarf plant (tt), giving 74 offspring. How many are expected to be dwarf?
items.e: Tt × tt gives 1 tall : 1 dwarf: 37.

items.q: What is non-disjunction?
c: chromosomes failing to separate in meiosis, giving gametes with an extra or missing chromosome
items.e: Trisomy 21 (Down syndrome) can result.

items.q: In pea, round (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r) and yellow (Y) over green (y). An RrYy × RrYy cross gives 112 seeds. How many are expected to be round and green?
items.e: The F₂ ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, so 3/16 of 112 = 21.

items.q: In pea, round (R) is dominant over wrinkled (r) and yellow (Y) over green (y). An RrYy × RrYy cross gives 64 seeds. How many are expected to be round and yellow?
items.e: The F₂ ratio is 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, so 9/16 of 64 = 36.

items.q: What is aneuploidy?
c: the gain or loss of one or a few chromosomes
items.e: Polyploidy is an increase in whole sets.

items.q: A dihybrid RrYy is test-crossed with rryy, giving 68 offspring. How many are expected to be wrinkled and green?
items.e: The test-cross ratio is 1 : 1 : 1 : 1, so 17.

items.q: What is the expected ratio of phenotypes from a cross between two heterozygotes (Aa × Aa) for a dominant trait?
items.e: The genotype ratio is 1 AA : 2 Aa : 1 aa.

items.e: The test-cross ratio is 1 : 1 : 1 : 1, so 21.

items.q: How does meiosis produce genetic variation?
c: by crossing over and independent assortment of homologous chromosomes
items.e: Random fertilisation adds more variation.

items.q: What is codominance?
c: both alleles are fully expressed in the heterozygote, such as blood group AB
items.e: Incomplete dominance gives a blend, such as pink flowers.

items.q: A dihybrid RrYy is test-crossed with rryy, giving 36 offspring. How many are expected to be wrinkled and green?

items.q: What is pleiotropy?
c: one gene affecting several characters, as in phenylketonuria
items.e: Polygenic inheritance is the reverse.

items.q: A colour-blind man and a woman who is not a carrier have a son. What is the chance the son is colour-blind?
c: 0, because the son gets his X chromosome from his mother
items.e: Fathers pass their Y to sons.

items.q: A cross expected to give a 1 : 2 : 1 ratio produced 41, 70, 49 offspring (total 160). Calculate χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E.
A chi-squared test is used on a cross expected to give five phenotype classes (5 categories). How many degrees of freedom are there?
items.e: Degrees of freedom = number of categories − 1 = 4.

items.q: A chi-squared test is used on a cross expected to give a 1 : 2 : 1 ratio (3 categories). How many degrees of freedom are there?
items.e: Degrees of freedom = number of categories − 1 = 2.

items.q: A cross expected to give a 3 : 1 ratio produced 86, 14 offspring (total 100). Calculate χ² = Σ(O − E)²/E.
A cross expected to give 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 produced 84, 30, 32, 14 (total 160). χ² = 2.13. The critical value at p = 0.05 is 7.82. What should you conclude?
c: the difference is significant, so the results do not fit the expected ratio
the difference is not significant; it is due to chance
the expected ratio is proved true
items.e: χ² = 2.13 is less than the critical value 7.82.
